The Commissioner vs K. Velan on 25 November, 2024 
Author: R. Suresh Kumar
Bench: R. Suresh Kumar, C. Saravanan
 W.A.No.
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras
 Dated: 25.11.2024
 Coram :
 The Honourable Mr.Justice R. Suresh Kumar
 And
 The Honourable Mr.Justice C. Saravanan
 W.A.No.1311 of 2024
 1. The Commissioner
 Food Safety and Drug Administration 
 Guindy, Chennai  32. 
 2. The Government Analyst
 Food Analysis Laboratory
 Guindy, Chennai  32.  .. Appel  Vs.
 K. Velan .. Respo  Prayer: Appeal filed under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent Act,
 against the order dated 30.10.2023 in W.P.No.16005 of 2022.
 For the Appellants : Mr.Kumaresan  Additional Advocate Gen  assisted by Mr.K.Tippu   Government Advocate  For the Respondent : Mr.S.Sivakumar  JUDGMENT (Order of the Court was made by R.SURESH KUMAR, J.) This intra-Court appeal has been directed against the order dated 30.10.2023 made in W.P.No.16005 of 2022. 
The Commissioner vs K. Velan on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57297622/
1 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.1. The respondent, who was the writ petitioner, was placed under suspension on 26.09.2019 for the reason that he indulged in a criminal case for the alleged offence punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Apart from the criminal case that was pending against him, Departmental Proceedings since has also been initiated, he was placed under suspension with effect from 26.09.2019 and he had been given subsistence allowance of 50% of his pay with effect from 24.09.2019 till 23.03.2020. Thereafter, the same was reduced to 25% with effect from 24.03.2020. 
2.2. Therefore, in order to get the enhanced subsistence allowance of 75%, after having made an attempt by making a representation, since the same did not provide any desired result, he approached this Court by filing W.P.No.10438 of 2021, where, the Writ Court, by order dated 06.04.2022, directed the employer to consider and decide the representation made by the writ petitioner dated 23.03.2021. 
2.3. Pursuant to the said directions issued by this Court, the employer, having considered the plea of the writ petitioner, passed orders on 03.06.2022, whereby, reiterated that proceedings under Rule 17(b) of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Discipline and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Appeals) Rules, 1955, is pending apart from the criminal case and in such circumstances, under F.R.53(1)(A)(iii) and as per the Government Letter dated 02.09.1976 , if the suspension is prolonged beyond six months' period, for which the direct reason is attributable to the Government servant,
then, the subsistence allowance can be reduced from 50% to 25%.
2.4. Therefore, citing this reason, the appellants justified the earlier reduction of subsistence allowance from 50% to 25% from 24.03.2020 and also by thus, rejecting the pea raised by the writ petitioner to enhance the subsistence allowance to 75%, through the order impugned dated 03.06.2022 before the Writ Court. 
2.5. When this was challenged, the learned Writ Court, having considered the circumstances,
concluded that though there has been an enabling provision under FR 53(1)(A)(i) and (1)(A)(ii),
whether there has been any reason to invoke such provision was the matter to be decided, where,
according to the learned Single Judge, no such reason has been stated by the employer before the Writ Court as to why the reduction of subsistence allowance into 25% from 50% and also denied the request of the petitioner to enhance the same to 75%. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.6 . Hence, the learned Single Judge was pleased to allow the said writ petition by setting aside the order dated 03.06.2022 and directed the employer to enhance the subsistence allowance to 75% from the date he has completed six months' period of the suspension. 
Thus, the said Writ Court order is impugned herein at the instance of the employer State in this intra-Court appeal. 
3.1. Mr.Kumaresan, learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the appellant State would contend that insofar as the reduction of subsistence allowance from 50% to 25% is concerned, since there has been a serious offence that has been committed by the respondent, as he is involved in a criminal case, which is punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and The Commissioner vs K. Velan on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57297622/ 
2 simultaneously, Departmental Proceedings also has been initiated, even though the Enquiry Officer was appointed, the enquiry could not be completed or proceeded further in view of the non-corporation on the part of the writ petitioner employee. 
3.2. Also, the learned Additional Government Pleader would submit that, simultaneously, the writ petitioner has moved this Court by filing W.P.No.28917 of 2022, seeking prohibition from p r o c e e d i n g f u r t h e r w i t h t h e e n q u i r y , s t a t i n g t h a t s i n c e t h e w i t n e s s e s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis both in the criminal case as well as in the Departmental Proceedings are one and the same , it may prejudice the interest of the employee, if the Departmental Proceedings is simultaneously permitted to proceed without awaiting the orders or judgment to be pronounced in the criminal case, which was pending before the concerned Court. 
Therefore, the learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the said plea though had been raised by both sides in the said writ petition, the learned Writ Court, though had permitted the employer to proceed with the enquiry, however, has given directions that the enquiry report shall be kept in abeyance until further orders of this Court and the said writ petition is still pending. Such an order was also passed by the Writ Court in yet another writ petition, which was also filed by the writ petitioner on 01.11.2022. Therefore, even though the State has completed the enquiry, could not proceed further with the same. 
3.3. The learned Additional Advocate General would therefore contend that these are all the actions taken on the part of the writ petitioner employee. Therefore, it can very well be construed that these actions are directly attributable for prolonging the suspension period beyond six months. Therefore,
on that ground also the writ petitioner is not entitled to get the benefit of subsistence allowance https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of 75% as has been sought. Therefore, there has been every justification on the part of the employer to reject the said plea through the impugned order before the Writ Court dated 03.06.2022. However, the same has been interfered by the learned Single Judge. Hence, the learned Additional Advocate General would seek indulgence of this Court in this intra-Court appeal. 
4.1. We have also heard Mr.S.Sivakumar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent employee,
who would submit that admittedly, the subsistence allowance has been reduced from 50% to 25%
with effect from 24.03.2020, but at that time, there was no writ petition or stay or any direction had been given to keep the Departmental Proceedings or the report of the Enquiry Officer pending. 
When that being so, absolutely there has been no reason on the part of the employer to reduce the subsistence allowance from 50% to 25%. 
4.2. That apart, he would further submit that when the request had been made to enhance the same to 75% and in this regard, a mandamus had been issued by this Court on 06.04.2022, even that was not considered in a proper perspective and they reiterated the earlier stand by citing F.R.53(1)(A)(iii). However, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis said Rule would not be invoked in the present circumstances of the case, since the issue has been considered threadbare by the learned Single Judge in the order impugned. 
The Commissioner vs K. Velan on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57297622/
3 4.3. Therefore, the counsel appearing for the respondent would submit that the order impugned does not warrant any interference at the hands of the Division Bench. Hence, he seeks dismissal of the writ petition. 
5. We have anxiously considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for both sides and have perused the materials placed on record. 
6.1. Insofar as the reduction of the subsistence allowance from 50% to 25% with effect from 24.03.2020, as admitted through the order before the Writ Court dated 03.06.2022, is concerned,
there has been no justification on the part of the employer. But, at the same time, at least within few months, there has been an order on 01.11.2022 in W.P.No.28917 of 2022 at the instance of the writ petitioner, where a prohibitory order has been issued by the Writ Court directing the employer to keep the enquiry report in abeyance and not to proceed further until further orders from this Court. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.2 . Therefore, one way or the other, there has been interference on the part of the respondent who came before this Court and got an order in his favour to stall the proceedings. These kinds of attempt made by the respondent, of course, resulted in the order dated 01.11.2022, which according to both sides still holds good or the reason could be attributable on the part of the writ petitioner. 
6.3. However, such reasons, emanating only with effect from 01.11.2022, but before that, no such reason could be found out from the records. Moreover, for the reduction of the subsistence allowance from 50% to 25% with effect from 24.03.2023, there is absolutely no reason as we found out earlier and therefore, such reduction taking effect from 24.03.2022 is unjustifiable. 
7. Resultantly, the order impugned passed by the Writ Court requires interference only by way of modification to the following effect:-
(i) The appellants are directed to enhance the subsistence allowance from 25% to 5 0 % w i t h e f f e c t f r o m 2 4 . 0 3 . 2 0 2 0 . H o w e v e r , f o r f u r t h e r https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis enhancement to 75%, the writ petitioner employee is not entitled to in view of the aforesaid reasons. 
(ii) Insofar as the enquiry is concerned, since it has been completed as stated by the learned Additional Advocate General, there can be no further impediment to proceed with the report of the Enquiry Officer, as the same could be placed before the Departmental Proceedings Authority, who in turn, can proceed further by giving a second opportunity to the employee to respond to the Enquiry Officer report and thereafter, let the Departmental Proceedings be concluded towards its logical conclusion in accordance with law. 
(iii) That proceedings can be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. Till such time, the writ petitioner is entitled for 50% of the subsistence allowance. It is upon the decision to be made in the ultimate Departmental Proceedings, further https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis course of action The Commissioner vs K. Velan on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57297622/
4 with regard to further enhancement of subsistence allowance could be decided by the employer. 
8. With these modifications of the order passed by the Writ Court dated 30.10.2023, this intra-Court appeal is disposed of. However, there shall be no order as to costs. Consequently, C.M.P.No.9507 of 2024 is closed.
